deep.reconstruction:
Context: this page continues Gauss's work on lemniscatic functions in terms of two entire (theta-type) functions P(φ), Q(φ). The previous page works with Q²±P² and the power-series coefficients of P², Q². The next page gives trigonometric parametrisations with x², 1±x⁴ and the coefficients 1−12+38−12+1, which appear on this page.

Setting (my reading). Put sl φ = P/Q. From sl²+cl²+sl²cl²=1 it follows that cl φ = √(Q²−P²)/√(Q²+P²). Each row n of the table lists four degree-n² homogeneous forms in P, Q. These are P(nφ), Q(nφ), √(Q²−P²)(nφ) and √(Q²+P²)(nφ), expressed through P=P(φ) and Q=Q(φ). Hence sl(nφ) = row[0]/row[1] and cl(nφ) = row[2]/row[3]. The multiplication formulas are thus written as polynomial (theta-type) identities rather than rational ones.

Top line. Gauss writes q(a−b)·q(a+b) = p(a)²p(b)² + q(a)²q(b)²; the second line restates it with the factors reordered. Lower-case p, q appear here to denote the functions P, Q.
- This is the addition theorem for the denominator function: Q(a+b)Q(a−b) = P(a)²P(b)² + Q(a)²Q(b)².
- It matches the denominator in sl(a+b)sl(a−b) = (sl²a − sl²b)/(1 + sl²a·sl²b). The numerator companion is P(a+b)P(a−b) = P(a)²Q(b)² − Q(a)²P(b)².
- Putting b=a and Q(0)=1 gives Q(2a) = Q⁴+P⁴, which is row 2.

Row 1: P, Q, √(QQ−PP), √(QQ+PP).

Row 2 (degree 4):
- P(2φ) = 2PQ√(Q⁴−P⁴).
- Q(2φ) = Q⁴+P⁴.
- Cosine numerator Q⁴−2Q²P²−P⁴; cosine denominator Q⁴+2Q²P²−P⁴.
- This is the classical duplication sl2u = 2s·c(1+s²)/(1+s⁴) and cl2u = (1−2s²−s⁴)/(1+2s²−s⁴), cleared of denominators.
- Consistency (my check): Q(2φ)² − P(2φ)² = (Q⁴−2Q²P²−P⁴)², and Q(2φ)² + P(2φ)² = (Q⁴+2Q²P²−P⁴)².

Row 3 (degree 9):
- P(3φ) = 3Q⁸P − 6Q⁴P⁵ − P⁹.
- Q(3φ) = Q⁹ + 6Q⁵P⁴ − 3QP⁸. A miswritten term was struck and rewritten.
- Cosine forms: √(Q²−P²)(Q⁸−4Q⁶P²−6Q⁴P⁴−4Q²P⁶+P⁸) and √(Q²+P²)(Q⁸+4Q⁶P²−6Q⁴P⁴+4Q²P⁶+P⁸).
- Hence sl3u = s(3−6s⁴−s⁸)/(1+6s⁴−3s⁸), the classical triplication.
- I verified by expansion that Q3² ∓ P3² equals (Q²∓P²)·(octic)².

Row 4 (degree 16):
- P(4φ) = 4PQ√(Q⁴−P⁴)(Q¹²−5Q⁸P⁴−5Q⁴P⁸+P¹²).
- Q(4φ) = Q¹⁶+20Q¹²P⁴−26Q⁸P⁸+20Q⁴P¹²+P¹⁶.
- Cosine numerator Q¹⁶−8Q¹⁴P²−12Q¹²P⁴−8Q¹⁰P⁶+38Q⁸P⁸+8Q⁶P¹⁰−12Q⁴P¹²+8Q²P¹⁴+P¹⁶; the denominator is the same with the signs of the odd-in-P² terms reversed.
- These follow from applying the row-2 formulas to row 2 (my derivation):
  - P4 = 2·P2·Q2·√(Q2⁴−P2⁴), where √(Q2⁴−P2⁴) = (Q⁴−2Q²P²−P⁴)(Q⁴+2Q²P²−P⁴) = Q⁸−6Q⁴P⁴+P⁸, and (Q⁴+P⁴)(Q⁸−6Q⁴P⁴+P⁸) = Q¹²−5Q⁸P⁴−5Q⁴P⁸+P¹².
  - Q4 = Q2⁴+P2⁴ = (Q⁴+P⁴)⁴ + 16P⁴Q⁴(Q⁴−P⁴)².
  - Cosine forms = Q2⁴ ∓ 2Q2²P2² − P2⁴.
- All of these I checked term by term.
- The palindromic coefficients 1, −12, 38, −12, 1 reappear on the next page, where the same quantities are converted to sin/cos of ½φ.

Right half (rotated, mixed hands). Numerical jottings unrelated to the lemniscate:
- 47, 48728, 50442, 52200, 53925 and 47814, 4737.1, 6354.
- 86.40, 85.70, 87.90, 86.25, and 86.56 = 90.72.
- 337.1, 331.3, 63.17, 64.75, 477.43, 486.77.
- Moon and star symbols, words like 'Jetzt' and 'Triumphus', large decorative letters.
- These are possibly astronomical, metrological or financial notes; not reconstructable as mathematics.
errors: No mathematical errors found in the four rows of multiplication formulas; all identities check (Q_n^2 ∓ P_n^2 equal the stated squares times (Q^2∓P^2), and the n=4 forms follow exactly from iterating n=2).
Row 3, second entry: the last term was first miswritten and corrected to −3QP^8 (a self-correction, not an error in the final text).

The top identity is written with lower-case p, q. If p, q meant the √(Q²∓P²) of the previous page, the formula would fail at b=a, since p⁴+q⁴ = 2(Q⁴+P⁴). It is correct when read as the P, Q functions, which is the consistent reading. The second line ('pb²:pa² + qb²:qa²') appears to be only a reordering, with ':' or '·' as multiplication.

results.what: Addition theorem for the lemniscatic denominator function: Q(a+b)Q(a−b) = P(a)²P(b)² + Q(a)²Q(b)²
results.modern_name: Theta-function addition formula (lemniscatic case), equivalent to sl(a+b)sl(a−b) = (sl²a−sl²b)/(1+sl²a sl²b)
results.usually_credited_to: Jacobi (theta function addition formulas, 1820s–1830s); Gauss's lemniscatic P, Q functions are documented in his Werke III

results.what: Duplication, triplication and quadruplication of the lemniscatic sine and cosine written as homogeneous polynomial identities of degree n² in P, Q
results.modern_name: Multiplication formulas for lemniscatic (elliptic) functions, theta-function form, division values / Abel's multiplication theorem
results.usually_credited_to: Fagnano (doubling of lemniscate arc, 1718), Euler (addition theorem, 1750s); multiplication in theta form Abel/Jacobi; Gauss's own lemniscatic work (1797–1800) is published in Werke III/X

deep.surprise_reason: Gauss's lemniscatic functions P, Q, his addition and multiplication formulas, and the series work (cf. previous page) are well documented in Werke III and X and in the Disquisitiones §335 remarks. This page is a clean worked table of n=1..4 multiplication forms, which is consistent with known material and is not new.
